294 km2 for 208-207, bbox 47.46-47.71 E, 38.48-38.67 N: a sliver in Iran, not a kingdom. The page has Armenia a Seleucid vassal from the end of 212 ('the country was divided into two kingdoms, both vassal states of the Seleucids') under Orontes IV until 200, then Seleucid rule 200-189; the shape to use for 210-189 is the new keyframe below.

correction.text: the 211 outline carried over 210-189; the 208 sliver is discarded

correction.text: Armenia as a Seleucid vassal kingdom, 210-189, with the 211 outline (the Seleucid dossier tints it)

keyframe_review.note: 224,603 km2 for 188-127: Artaxias I and Zariadres became autonomous kings after Magnesia (190) and were 'recognized as such by the Roman Senate according to the Treaty of Apamea in 188 BC' (Artaxiad page). The page does not describe Artaxias's frontiers; outline stands.
224,379 km2 for 126-111: Artavasdes I and Tigranes I appear in the Artaxiad list with no dates or events; unverified.

132,054 km2 for 110-92, bbox east edge down from 48.93 to 44.87 E: the east is lost. The Tigranes page dates the Parthian cession of the 'seventy valleys' in the Caspiane to c. 96/95 BC (the year Mithridates II released Tigranes), not 110, and says Tigranes 'would remain a Parthian vassal until the late 80s BC'. Cliopatria's loss is larger and 15 years earlier than anything on the page; the shape stands and the ledger carries both the Cliopatria change (110, confidence 1) and the page's 95. From -95 to -92 this outline is extended by the Sophene gain of /ledger/8 (new keyframe kingdom-of-armenia_-95): the 110 outline holds only 22 of Sophene's 97 cells (75 cells, about 19,000 km2, lie outside it).

correction.text: the 110 outline plus the Kingdom of Sophene, whose last king Artanes Tigranes 'deposed' (year 95 from the Orontid page's infobox 'Dissolution: 95 BC' and the kingdom-of-sophene dossier; the Tigranes page, re-read 2026-10-31, gives no year)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (review eu-19-a): the /ledger/8 gain of Sophene (about 19,000 km2 outside the 110 and 91 outlines) had no trace in the keyframes, so Sophene would have been Armenian in 95-92, not in 91-88 and Armenian again from 87 with no loss between. The Tigranes page: 'He deposed Artanes, the last king of the Kingdom of Sophene'; the Kingdom page has the peak 'from 83 to 69 BC' after Armenia 'reincorporated Sophene'.

130,870 km2 for 91-88: Armenia as a Parthian vassal; nothing else on the pages. Adjusted (review eu-19-a): the Cliopatria outline lacks 75 of Sophene's 97 cells (about 19,000 km2), which Armenia absorbed in 95 and nothing returns, so Sophene is added.

correction.text: the 91 outline plus Sophene, absorbed in 95 (/ledger/8) and kept: no page records a loss of it before the 87 outline, which holds most of Sophene again

keyframe_review.note: 300,627 km2 for 87-78, bbox south to 36.67 N and east again to 48.93 E: 'Between 88 and 85 BC, he retook Adiabene, Gordyene, and Media Atropatene' (Tigranes page). The shape has no Syria, which the Kingdom page enters in 83 BC, so this verdict ends the shape in 84 (years only, shape unchanged); 83-78 is the next entry. The -87 gain of Media Atropatene (/ledger/9) is the part of the region inside this outline (about 44,000 of 125,400 km2); the page gives no extent, so no union with the whole region is made. About 3,800 km2 of Sophene (15 cells) also lie outside this outline.

correction.text: shape unchanged, valid -87 to -84; Syria, Phoenicia and Cilicia follow in 83

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Kingdom page has 'Tigranes enters Syria' in 83 BC and the peak 'from 83 to 69 BC', and the Tigranes page says he 'conquered Phoenicia and Cilicia, effectively putting an end to the last remnants of the Seleucid Empire' after 83. Cliopatria shows these only from 77. Cliopatria's last Seleucid shape (91-78, 88,974 km2) is the Syrian rump he took, so the 83-78 outline is the 87 shape plus that rump. Phoenicia and Cilicia are undated beyond 'after 83', so their inclusion from 83 is a simplification.

correction.text: Greater Armenia plus the Seleucid rump kingdom: 'the Syrians decided to choose Tigranes as the protector of their kingdom and offered him the crown of Syria' (83 BC), then Phoenicia and Cilicia

keyframe_review.note: 519,631 km2 for 77-67 (bbox 34.08-48.93 E, 32.75-41.65 N). The Tigranes page says 'At its peak, his empire covered a territory of 900,000 km2' (the Kingdom infobox: about 900,000 km2 c. 70 BC): the shape is 0.58 of the figure, within a factor of two, so the shape stands. The southern limit fits 'The southern border of his domain reached as far as Ptolemais'. The step from the 83-78 outline (about 389,000 km2) to this one is the undated 'Large territories were taken from the Parthians' (Artaxiad page). The page dates Lucullus's victory at Tigranocerta to 6 October 69 and Artaxata to 68, but not the loss of Syria, so the shape's 67 end is unverified. Repair (review eu-19-a): this verdict covers -77 to -70 as drawn. From 69 the Syrian and Phoenician rump goes to the restored Seleucid kingdom (ledger -69; Kingdom page peak 'from 83 to 69 BC'; Seleucid Empire page: 'a rump Seleucid kingdom was restored' after Lucullus' victory in 69), so -69 to -67 is the new keyframe kingdom-of-armenia_-69.

correction.text: the 77 outline without the Syrian and Phoenician rump that the restored Seleucid kingdom of Antiochus XIII takes in 69

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (review eu-19-a): the 77 outline kept Syria to 67, but the Kingdom page ends the peak in 69 and seleucid-empire /ledger/83 (Seleucid Empire page) restores the rump in 69. The Cliopatria Seleucid shape of 66-64 (70,000 km2) overlaps the 77 outline on about 66,000 km2; the rest of the 77 outline stands to 67 (the page dates Tigranocerta to 69 and Artaxata to 68 but no further loss before 66).

168,773 km2 for 66-64: 'Pompey allowed him to retain his kingdom shorn of his conquests', and 'all of his conquests were annexed' (Tigranes page); Armenia a Roman client from 66-65 (Roman Armenia page).

217,689 km2 for 63 BC to AD 59 (the same outline as the 188 shape). region.text: the Satrapy of Armenia, Orontes III's

ledger.note: 331: Orontes III's Armenia emerges from the Achaemenid collapse. 'defeated at the Battle of Gaugamela in 331 BC' and infobox 'Reign of Orontes III begins: 331 BC'; the satrapy itself dates from 'c. 533 BC'. The page names no territory; the Armenian Highlands is the region reading. Cliopatria draws the state from 326.

321: the satrapy becomes a kingdom. Kingdom page, 321 BC: the satrapy becomes a kingdom under the Orontids, who return as kings after Neoptolemus dies; Orontid page: 'the Kingdom of Armenia from 321 BC to 200 BC'.

region.text: Sophene, the Orontid lands round Arsamosata

ledger.note: c. 260: Sophene becomes a separate kingdom. Orontid infobox 'Founded ... 260 BC (Sophene)', with 'Sames of Sophene (c. 260 BC) and Arsames I (260–228 BC)'. The same page says 'Towards the end of 212 BC the country was divided into two kingdoms, both vassal states of the Seleucids'; Cliopatria separates Sophene in 256 (the kingdom-of-sophene dossier uses 256).
210: the capital moves from Armavir to Yervandashat. Infobox 'Armavir (331–210 BC), Yervandashat (210–176 BC)'.

200: Artaxias I overthrows Orontes IV; the Artaxiad dynasty replaces the Orontids. Kingdom page, 201/200 BC: Orontes IV is overthrown and Artaxias I takes over; the Orontid page has 'the overthrow of Orontes IV and the accession of Artaxias I to the throne of Armenia in the early 2nd century BC' and lists 'Seleucid rule (200–189 BC)' and the Artaxiad page 'Founded: 190 BC'. After Magnesia (190) Artaxias and Zariadres became autonomous kings and were recognised by the Senate at Apamea in 188 (Artaxiad page); the Seleucid dossier carries the vassal tint to 188.
176: the capital moves to Artaxata (Artashat). Infobox 'Artaxata (176–77 BC; 69 BC–120 AD)'; the same page has 'Artashes I founds Artashat in 185 BC'.

region.text: the eastern part of the 111 outline that Cliopatria no longer draws from 110

ledger.note: c. 110: the east is lost to Parthia. The Tigranes page dates no loss in 110; the date is the Cliopatria change (224,379 to 132,054 km2, east edge from 48.93 to 44.87 E). The parthian-empire dossier has Armenia a Parthian vassal from 120. Bridging judgment: the page has Tigranes 'a hostage at the Parthian court until c. 96/95 BC'.

region.text: the 'seventy valleys' in the Caspiane (nearest gazetteer region: Arran)

ledger.note: c. 95: Tigranes cedes the 'seventy valleys'. 'Tigranes ceded an area called "seventy valleys" in the Caspiane to Mithridates II' when released c. 96/95 (page); 'When he acquired power, he recovered these valleys'. The page does not date the cession itself; the year is the release. The valleys lie in the east, probably already outside the 110 outline.

region.text: the Kingdom of Sophene, whose last king Artanes he deposed

ledger.note: c. 95: Sophene is absorbed. 'He deposed Artanes, the last king of the Kingdom of Sophene' (Tigranes page, undated); the Orontid page's infobox gives Sophene's 'Dissolution: 95 BC' and the kingdom-of-sophene dossier uses 95.

region.text: Media Atropatene, 'retook[en]' (the part inside the 87 outline)

ledger.note: 87: Atropatene is retaken. 'Between 88 and 85 BC, he retook Adiabene, Gordyene, and Media Atropatene' (the year is inside the page's span and is Cliopatria's change to 300,627 km2). Repair (review eu-19-a): the region was all of Atropatene, but the 87 outline holds only 174 cells (about 44,000 km2) of its 496 (about 125,400 km2); 322 cells (about 81,400 km2) lie outside. The Tigranes page (re-read 2026-10-31) says only 'Between 88 and 85 BC, he retook Adiabene, Gordyene, and Media Atropatene' and gives no territorial detail for Atropatene, so the gain is cut to the part the standard outline draws; the further Atropatene land in the 77 outline comes with /ledger/14 (confidence 1). Residual: about 9,100 km2 of the Adiabene gain (/ledger/11) also lie outside the 87 outline.

region.text: Gordyene (Corduene)

ledger.note: 87: Gordyene is retaken, in the same sentence ('Between 88 and 85 BC'). The kingdom-of-gordyene dossier has it a vassal of Armenia from 87.

region.text: Adiabene

ledger.note: 87: Adiabene is retaken, in the same sentence ('Between 88 and 85 BC'). The kingdom-of-adiabene dossier has it a vassal of Armenia from 87; the parthian-empire dossier records the loss of Adiabene and Gordyene in 87.

region.text: Syria, Phoenicia and Cilicia, the Seleucid rump

ledger.note: 83: Tigranes becomes king of Syria. Kingdom page: Tigranes enters Syria in 83 and the peak runs 'from 83 to 69 BC'; 'the Syrians decided to choose Tigranes as the protector of their kingdom and offered him the crown of Syria', 'He then conquered Phoenicia and Cilicia, effectively putting an end to the last remnants of the Seleucid Empire' (Tigranes page, no year for the last two); the seleucid-empire dossier has the whole rump lost in 83.

77: the capital moves to the new city of Tigranocerta. Infobox 'Tigranocerta (77–69 BC)'; the Tigranes page says 'Many of the inhabitants of conquered cities were sent to his new metropolis of Tigranocerta' without a year.

region.text: the territories taken from Parthia (Mesopotamia and the south-east) and the Albanian and Iberian borderlands, as drawn in Cliopatria's 77 outline

ledger.note: c. 77: the rest of the empire. Cliopatria's 77 outline (519,631 km2) is about 130,000 km2 larger than the 87 outline plus the Seleucid rump. The Artaxiad page says only: 'Large territories were taken from the Parthians, who were forced to sign a treaty of friendship with Tigranes' and 'Iberia, Albania, and Atropatene also lost territories' (both undated); the Tigranes page has the empire stretch 'from the Caspian Sea to the Mediterranean'. The parthian-empire dossier records Mesopotamia going back to Parthia in 66. Bridging judgment, dated by the Cliopatria change.
69: the capital returns to Artaxata after Tigranocerta falls. Infobox 'Artaxata (176–77 BC; 69 BC–120 AD)'.

region.text: the Syrian and Phoenician rump of Antiochus XIII

ledger.note: 69: Syria slips away and a Seleucid rump is restored. The Kingdom page (re-read 2026-10-31) ends the peak in 69, 'from 83 to 69 BC', but does not name Lucullus or Syria; the Seleucid Empire page (read 2026-10-31) has 'Following the Roman general Lucullus' defeat of both Mithridates and Tigranes in 69 BC, a rump Seleucid kingdom was restored under Antiochus XIII.' The Tigranes page is silent on how or when Syria was lost. The year is the pages', the land is the Seleucid rump of seleucid-empire /ledger/83 (the mirror, same region). Repair (review eu-19-a): the keyframe 77 outline used to keep Syria to 67.

region.text: Greater Armenia, Tigranocerta and Artaxata

ledger.note: 69, 6 October: Lucullus beats Tigranes at Tigranocerta. 'On October 6, 69 BC, Tigranes' much larger force was decisively defeated by the Roman army under Lucullus'; Artaxata followed on 6 October 68. The Kingdom page says the kingdom was 'conquered by Rome in 69 BC'. The roman-republic dossier opens its contest in 69.

region.text: Greater Armenia

ledger.note: 66: Tigranes surrenders to Pompey. 'In 66 BC, Pompey advanced into Armenia with Tigranes the Younger, and Tigranes ... surrendered.'

region.text: the conquests still held in 66: Mesopotamia, the eastern provinces and whatever of Syria, Phoenicia and Cilicia lay outside the Seleucid rump lost in 69

ledger.note: 66: the empire is stripped. 'Pompey allowed him to retain his kingdom shorn of his conquests'; 'all of his conquests were annexed'; he paid 6,000 talents. The parthian-empire dossier has Mesopotamia going to Parthia in 66 and the seleucid-empire one a Roman annexation of Syria in 64, so the counterpart split is the neighbours' reading; this page names only the loss. Repair (review eu-19-a): the Syrian and Phoenician rump is no longer in this loss, because /ledger (-69) gives it to the Seleucid kingdom three years earlier.

region.text: the western edge restored in 63, not described on the pages

ledger.note: 63: the outline widens again in the west. The Roman Armenia page has Armenia 'made a Roman client kingdom by Pompey in 66–65 BC'; no page opened gives the territory, and the return of the standard 217,689 km2 outline from 168,773 km2 is the Cliopatria change (west edge 40.48 to 38.74 E). Bridging judgment.

region.text: Greater Armenia

ledger.note: 34: Mark Antony invades Armenia. 'Mark Antony invaded and defeated the kingdom in 34 BC' (Kingdom page; the Artaxiad page has 35, and Artavasdes II sent captive to Egypt). The roman-republic dossier records an occupation 34-32.

region.text: Greater Armenia

ledger.note: 34: the invasion is over in the year it began; the pages record the defeat of the kingdom and nothing later until Augustus's 20 BC truce with Parthia, which made Armenia 'a buffer zone'.
12: the last Artaxiad kings are overthrown ('overthrown in 12 AD', Kingdom page lead); the Arsacid page has 'The first appearance of an Arsacid on the Armenian throne occurred in 12' (Vonones I).

52: Tiridates I founds the Arsacid dynasty of Armenia (Kingdom page: Tiridates I is proclaimed king in 52 AD, founding the Arsacid dynasty); the Roman-Parthian War page has the Parthians installing him 'in 52/53' and Armenia a Roman client of Nero's from the 66 coronation.

region.text: Armenia, the zone between Rome and Parthia

ledger.note: 58: Rome and Parthia fight over Armenia. 'Tension mounted and finally, in the early spring of 58, war broke out'; 'In 59, the Romans marched to the south, towards Tigranocerta'; the Kingdom page has Tigranes VI installed in 58, the Romans gaining Armenia in 60 and losing it in 62, and the Arsacid page the 'Battle of Rhandeia in 62'.

region.text: Armenia

ledger.note: 63: the Treaty of Rhandeia (Kingdom page): Arsacid members rule Armenia as Roman client kings; Tiridates went to Rome and was crowned by Nero in 66.

region.text: Armenia, made a Roman province

ledger.note: 114: Trajan annexes Armenia. 'In 114, Emperor Trajan incorporated Armenia into the Empire, making it a full Roman province' and deposed Parthamasiris; the province 'reached the shores of the Caspian Sea'.

region.text: Armenia restored as a kingdom

ledger.note: 118: Hadrian gives Armenia up. 'In 118, Hadrian gave Armenia up, and installed Parthamaspates as its king' (Trajan died in August 117; the roman-empire dossier dates its loss to 117).

120: the capital moves to Vagharshapat. Infobox 'Vagharshapat (120–330)'. The Roman-Parthian War of 161-166 page says only that 'In 164, a new capital, Kaine Polis (New City in Greek), replaced Artaxata'.

region.text: Armenia

ledger.note: 161: Vologases IV invades Armenia. 'Vologases IV of Parthia, made his move in late summer or early autumn 161' and 'Vologases entered the Kingdom of Armenia ... expelled its king and installed his own'; Rome's counter-attack under Statius Priscus won in 163 with the capture of Artaxata.

region.text: Armenia

ledger.note: 164: Rome reinstalls its king. 'A new king was installed: a Roman senator of consular rank and Arsacid descent, C. Iulius Sohaemus', 'Rex Armeniis Datus' on the coinage of 164; the capital becomes Kaine Polis.

region.text: Armenia, occupied by the Sasanians from 252

ledger.note: 252: the Sasanian Persians occupy Armenia (Kingdom page, 252 AD); 'after which Shapur laid waste to the country' (Arsacid page, after Barbalissos, c. 252); the sasanian-empire dossier dates the gain to 253. The Narseh page has 'all of Armenia (since 252) were under Iranian rule'.

region.text: Armenia

ledger.note: 287: Tiridates III returns with Roman armies (Kingdom page, 287 AD: he is brought to power by Roman armies; the infobox gives his reign as 298-330 and the Narseh page restores him only after Satala; the sasanian-empire dossier has the loss in 299). Cliopatria's shape begins in 287.

region.text: Armenia 'extended up to the fortress of Zintha, in Media'

ledger.note: 298/9: the Peace of Nisibis. 'The semi-independent kingdom of Armenia was to be extended up to the fortress of Zintha, in Media'; Iran was 'to relinquish all her rights over Iberia' and five provinces beyond the Tigris went to Rome ('Peace of Nisibis (299)'). Cliopatria's outline does not change, so the standard outline already reaches Media Atropatene. Repair (review eu-19-a): the region was all of Atropatene (496 cells, about 125,400 km2); the page gives only 'up to the fortress of Zintha, in Media' (re-read 2026-10-31, no year of its own, no extent), so the gain is now the part of Atropatene inside the 287/306 outline (180 cells, about 45,500 km2), which is already Armenian from /ledger/32; about 79,900 km2 of the region lie outside both shapes and are not claimed. Zintha is not in the gazetteer (see notes), so no radius is used. Confidence stays 2.
336: the capital moves to Dvin. Infobox 'Dvin (336–428)'; text: 'Khosrov III builds Dvin' in 335.

region.text: Armenia

ledger.note: 368: Shapur II conquers Armenia. 'Sassanid conquest (Shapur II) 368–370' (Arsacid page); 'After eliminating Arshak, Shapur laid waste to Armenia, destroying its major cities' (Arshak II page: 'Armenia was left to fend for itself' after Jovian's 363 peace, Arshak held at the 'Castle of Oblivion' in 369/370).

region.text: Armenia

ledger.note: 370/371: Pap restores the kingdom. Pap 'returned to Armenia to take the throne with the help of the emperor Valens in 370/371'; the sasanian-empire dossier has the contest end in 371.

region.text: the smaller Roman share west of the line 'running from Erzurum to Mush': 'the Romans retained Sophene and a smaller portion of Armenia'

ledger.note: 387: Armenia is partitioned between Rome and Persia. 'The Sassanids received the larger share called Persarmenia, while the Romans retained Sophene and a smaller portion of Armenia'; the line ran 'from Erzurum to Mush' ('resolved in 384 and again in 387'). 'Members of the Arsacid dynasty continued to rule both portions.'

region.text: the south-eastern and eastern strip that Cliopatria's 387 outline no longer includes (east of 47.12 E)

ledger.note: 387: the eastern strip that Cliopatria's 387 shape drops (to 47.12 E) falls with the Persian share. The page gives no eastern limit; the sasanian-empire dossier has the eastern part a Sasanian vassal from 387. Bridging judgment.

region.text: the Persian share of Armenia

ledger.note: 428: the Arsacid kingdom is abolished. 'In 428, Armenian nobles petitioned Bahram V to depose Artaxias IV'; 'Bahram V abolished the Kingdom of Armenia and appointed Veh Mihr Shapur as marzban'. Persian Armenia becomes the Marzpanate; Cliopatria keeps an Armenia shape to 489 and again 638-646 (see keyframes).

wars.name: Antiochus III's campaign in Armenia and Sophene
wars.outcome: Antiochus III besieged Arsamosata; Xerxes of Sophene and Commagene surrendered and the country was divided into two kingdoms, both Seleucid vassals.
wars.note: 'Antiochus III the Great decided to suppress the local dynasties, and besieged Arsamosata'; 'Towards the end of 212 BC the country was divided into two kingdoms, both vassal states of the Seleucids'. No border moved on the pages; the Seleucid dossier records the vassal tint (212 to 188).

wars.name: Tigranes the Great's conquests
wars.outcome: Tigranes retook Adiabene, Gordyene and Media Atropatene (88-85), then took the Seleucid rump in 83 and 'conquered Phoenicia and Cilicia'; his empire reached from the Caspian to the Mediterranean.
wars.note: 'Between 88 and 85 BC, he retook Adiabene, Gordyene, and Media Atropatene'; Syria in 83. Large territories were also 'taken from the Parthians, who were forced to sign a treaty of friendship' (undated).

wars.name: Third Mithridatic War, Roman invasions of Armenia
wars.outcome: Lucullus beat Tigranes at Tigranocerta (6 October 69) and reached Artaxata (6 October 68); Pompey forced his surrender in 66 and left him Armenia 'shorn of his conquests' for 6,000 talents.
wars.note: The Tigranes page does not name the Third Mithridatic War; it has Tigranes agreeing with Mithridates VI 'to extend his influence in the East, while Mithridates set to conquer Roman land in Asia Minor'.

wars.name: Mark Antony's invasion of Armenia
wars.outcome: Antony invaded and defeated the kingdom in 34 BC and sent Artavasdes II to Egypt, where he was executed.
wars.note: The Artaxiad page has 35 BC for the invasion and the Kingdom page 34 BC. Augustus's truce with Parthia in 20 BC made Armenia 'a buffer zone'.

wars.name: Roman-Parthian War of 58-63
wars.outcome: Rome marched on Tigranocerta in 59, lost the Battle of Rhandeia in 62, and in 63 the settlement made the Arsacid Tiridates a Roman client king; he was crowned by Nero in Rome in 66.
wars.note: Page dates: war from early spring 58, Tigranocerta in 59, war resumed in the spring of 62, Parthian delegation to Rome in the spring of 63, coronation in 66; Artaxata is not dated.

wars.name: Trajan's annexation of Armenia
wars.outcome: Trajan deposed Parthamasiris and made Armenia a Roman province in 114; Hadrian gave it up in 118 and installed Parthamaspates.
wars.note: The roman-empire dossier dates the loss to 117 (Trajan died in August 117); the page says 118 for Hadrian's act.

wars.name: Roman-Parthian War of 161-166
wars.outcome: Vologases IV invaded Armenia in 161; Statius Priscus took Artaxata in 163 and Sohaemus was installed in 164; Rome then went down the Euphrates to Dura-Europos and sacked Ctesiphon and Seleucia (165), the war ending in 166 with Roman gains in upper Mesopotamia.
wars.note: Armenia fell to Parthia in 161 and returned to Rome's nominee in 164.

wars.name: Sasanian conquest of Armenia
wars.outcome: The Sasanian Persians occupied Armenia in 252, after Barbalissos; Armenia stayed under Iranian rule until Tiridates III's restoration (287 or 298/9).
wars.note: Narseh governed Armenia as 'Vazurg Šāh Arminān' (Narseh page, reign-table 271-293).

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian war of 296-298

zones.text: Armenia extended 'up to the fortress of Zintha, in Media'

wars.outcome: Galerius beat Narseh at Satala in 298; the Peace of Nisibis (298/9) gave Rome five provinces beyond the Tigris, extended Armenia to Zintha in Media and Tiridates III was reinstated.
wars.note: 'In 296 or 297, Narseh's forces inflicted a defeat on' Galerius; 'Galerius made preparations throughout the winter of 297 and invaded Armenia with 25,000 men'.

wars.name: Shapur II's conquest of Armenia
wars.outcome: Shapur II laid waste to Armenia and held Arshak II captive; Pap regained the throne with Valens's help in 370/371.
wars.note: 'Sassanid conquest (Shapur II) 368–370'; the Arshak II page puts Arshak's capture in 369 or 370 and the Roman cession of 363 as the cause.

wars.name: Partition of Armenia between Rome and Persia

zones.text: the smaller Roman share west of the line 'running from Erzurum to Mush': 'the Romans retained Sophene and a smaller portion of Armenia'

wars.outcome: Persia received the larger share (Persarmenia), Rome Sophene and a smaller portion, on a line from Erzurum to Mush.
wars.note: 'resolved in 384 and again in 387'; the Roman Armenia page calls it the 'Peace of Acilisene (usually dated c. 387)' with 'about four fifths' under Persian rule.

certainty.note: Armenian frontiers are known from historians and the Roman-Parthian settlements, not from survey lines; the Tigris-side districts after the 298/9 peace and Rome's border at the Euphrates were negotiated but their lines are not on the pages.
The Roman-Persian line 'from Erzurum to Mush' (387) is the only treaty-drawn frontier on the pages and could be drawn sharply as a segment; every other edge stays soft.

notes: Cliopatria row Kingdom of Armenia (-326..646, 32 shapes) is split: this dossier is the kingdom, -331..428 (Orontid, Artaxiad, Arsacid; the dynasty changes are rename events). The shapes after 428 are not this state: 451-489 is the Sasanian Marzpanate (verdict wrong: no Armenian state; the sasanian-empire dossier should hold the land) and 638-646 is the Principality of Armenia under Theodore Rshtuni (verdict adjust, status change only; the principality, 628/638 to 884, needs its own dossier, suggested slug principality-of-armenia, with the Emirate of Armenia from 654; nothing in this batch writes it). Cliopatria has no shape for 490-637 and 647-885. Page budget (14) spent on: Kingdom of Armenia (antiquity), Orontid dynasty, Artaxiad dynasty, Tigranes the Great, Roman-Parthian War of 58-63, Arsacid dynasty of Armenia, Roman Armenia, Marzpanate period, Muslim conquest of Armenia, Peace of Acilisene, Roman-Parthian War of 161-166, Principality of Armenia, Arshak II, Narseh. Pages that would not load: Partition_of_Armenia_(387), Peace_of_Nisibis_(298), Arshak_II_of_Armenia (url_not_found; replaced by Peace_of_Acilisene, Narseh and Arshak_II). Shape fixes: the 208-207 sliver (294 km2) is wrong and 210-189 is bridged; 60-67, 118-153, 161-164, 371-386 are bridged because the kingdom continued while Cliopatria shows nothing; 114-117 (Roman province) and 252-286 (Sasanian) have no Armenian shape on purpose; 83-78 adds the Seleucid rump to the 87 outline for Tigranes's Syria; the 331-327 keyframe carries the 326 outline back to Orontes III. Areas: the Tigranes page and Kingdom infobox give 900,000 km2 for the peak (Cliopatria 519,631, ratio 0.58) and 311,000 km2 c. 300 AD (218,561, ratio 0.70); both within a factor of two. Disagreements: Artaxiad dynasty founded 189 (lead) or 190 (infobox); Sophene split 260 (Orontid infobox) or 212 (Orontid text) or 256 (Cliopatria and the kingdom-of-sophene dossier); Antony 35 (Artaxiad) or 34 (Kingdom); Tiridates III restored 287 (Kingdom, Arsacid) or after 298 (Narseh); capital Vagharshapat 120 (infobox) or Kaine Polis 164 (war page); Dvin 335 or 336; Roman loss of Armenia 117 (roman-empire dossier) or 118 (page); Sasanian gain 253 (sasanian-empire dossier) or 252. Gaps, all page-silent: the Orontid and early Artaxiad frontiers; the 63 BC widening of the outline; the Cliopatria loss of the east in 110 (page: c. 96/95); Artaxias I's conquests; Tigranes's territory by year (Cilicia and Phoenicia 'after 83'); the Kharput/Sophene boundary; the 3rd-century Sasanian occupation's extent. Vassal tints are held in the suzerains' dossiers (seleucid-empire 212-188, parthian-empire from 120 to 87, roman-republic from 66, roman-empire from AD 1, sasanian-empire from 387); no vassal event of Armenia's own is recorded because the pages opened name no Armenian vassal. Gazetteer names needed: Caspiane (region, the Kura mouth side of Albania; Arran used), Zintha/Ziatha (place, in Media), Tigranocerta (place, disputed site near Silvan), Yervandashat (place, Araxes plain), Armavir and Dvin (ancient sites; the gazetteer has only the Armenia admin1 and the Russian Armavir). Capital coordinates are approximate and flagged in the capitals' notes. Counterparts needing dossiers: Marzpanate of Armenia (428 to c. 636, Sasanian province), Principality of Armenia (628/638-884), Diauehi and Sophene-linked Commagene are covered by other rows. The kingdom-of-sophene dossier records its 256 foundation as 'split from Orontid Armenia' and its 95 end as a hand-over to this state; the parthian-empire dossier has Armenia a vassal from 120 (Artavasdes I), which no page opened here confirms. Repair 2026-10-31 (review eu-19-a): (1) /ledger/33 (299) and /ledger/9 (-87) are cut to the part of Atropatene inside the 287 and -87 outlines (the pages give no extent for Media Atropatene or beyond 'Zintha'); the 79,900 km2 of the region outside the 287/306 shape and the 81,400 km2 outside the -87 shape are not claimed. (2) New keyframes kingdom-of-armenia_-95 (Sophene added, -95..-92) and kingdom-of-armenia_-69 (Syrian rump removed, -69..-67); the -91 keyframe is adjusted to keep Sophene. (3) The 69 loss of Syria to the restored Seleucid rump is ledger-new (Kingdom page peak 'from 83 to 69 BC'; Seleucid Empire page for the rump) and the -66 loss to Rome no longer includes that rump. (4) The 638 and 644 shapes are verdict wrong, like 451. (5) Rulers: Artavasdes I and Tigranes I (undated, one entry), Ariobarzanes, Artavasdes IV, Vonones I to Mithridates (12-52), Tigranes VI, Pacorus, Vologases II, Khosrov I and IV, and Shapur are added; Tiridates III starts in 287. Interregna kept open because the pages name no Armenian king: 200-190 BC (Orontid list ends 200, Artaxias I from 190), 114-117 (Roman province), 252-287 (Sasanian) and 368-370 (Sasanian conquest). Residual: about 9,100 km2 of the Adiabene gain of 87 (/ledger/11) lie outside the -87 outline; the pages give no better extent.
